articles.title: A Multimodal Framework for Measuring Creator Communication on Short-Form Video
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.33043v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Short-form video combines speech, imagery, and on-screen text, creating challenges for systematic content analysis. We present a five-stage multimodal framework for measuring creators' themes and communication strategies at scale. The framework integrates platform metadata, speech transcripts, and vision-language descriptions of sampled frames, then applies large language models to generate predefined indicators and open-ended labels. articles.title: The Capability Transfer: Cohort Reversal, Codified Expertise, and the Adaptability Tax of AI Transformation
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.33102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Most analyses of AI and employment ask which jobs are exposed. This paper asks what happens to the pipeline that produces experts. It extends the model of Caosun and Aral (2026) from a single worker to a firm with two cohorts, juniors and seniors, and studies how expertise formation changes when codified work is automated. articles.summary: arXiv:2610.33243v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Despite a ban on the international trading of recently poached ivory, elephants are still killed for their tusks. Ivory and its products are mainly sold in online marketplaces. articles.title: Propasafe-Hybrid: A Text-Based Hybrid Propaganda Detection Tool
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.33464v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Propagandistic content increasingly circulates through online news and social media, where readers often encounter it with limited scrutiny, highlighting the need for reliable and fine-grained detection. This paper introduces Propasafe-Hybrid, a sentence-level system that integrates a fine-tuned transformer classifier with LLM-based technique classification to identify, label, and explain specific propaganda strategies. articles.title: FraudSociety: A Generative Agent-Based Society for the Financial-Fraud Economy
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.33536v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Financial fraud caused over \$15.9 billion in losses in the United States in 2025, according to the Federal Trade Commission~\citep{ftc2026databook}. Understanding such large-scale harm requires jointly modeling informational and financial dynamics. Yet existing simulators typically capture only one side of this interaction, leaving a gap in modeling how fraud unfolds in the real world. articles.title: Gender Associations in LLM-Mediated ADHD Self-Diagnosis
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.33697v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for medical self-diagnosis. However, the way demographic cues shape outputs in these interactions remains poorly understood. This is particularly consequential for diagnoses like ADHD, where persistent gender disparities are not fully aligned with the clinical evidence. articles.title: The Conditional Value of Costly Information in Collective-Risk Dilemmas
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.33895v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many high-stakes collective problems, e.g., climate mitigation and pandemic response, share a structure in which risk materializes unless a group threshold is met. This threshold is often uncertain, but uncertainty can be reduced at a cost.
